definitions.explanation: The act of putting a law, regulation, or policy into effect. Commonly used in legal and governmental contexts.

examples.japanese: この{法律|ほうりつ}は{来月|らいげつ}から{施行|しこう}される。
examples.english: This law will be enforced starting next month.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{規制|きせい}の{施行|しこう}{日|び}が{決|き}まった。
examples.english: The enforcement date for the new regulation has been decided.

examples.japanese: {条例|じょうれい}の{施行|しこう}により、{喫煙|きつえん}が{禁止|きんし}された。
examples.english: Smoking was banned through the enforcement of the ordinance.

notes:
READING NOTE:
In legal contexts, this word is read しこう. However, a related word {施工|せこう} (construction work) exists with a different reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{施行|しこう}する (to enforce, to implement)
・{施行|しこう}{日|び} (enforcement date)
・{施行|しこう}{規則|きそく} (enforcement regulations)
・{即日|そくじつ}{施行|しこう} (immediate enforcement)

RELATED TERMS:
・{公布|こうふ} (promulgation) - announcing a law
・{施行|しこう} (enforcement) - putting a law into effect
・{廃止|はいし} (abolition) - ending a law
